name: NY-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+22
Incumbent Yvette Clarke seeking re-election with a large fundraising edge
No competitive polling or expert ratings, but prediction markets price a Democratic win near certain
Republican challenger Joel Azumah has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Clarke: a D+22 district, incumbency, and a roughly $1 million fundraising advantage over a challenger with no reported money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending against Clarke would be the main thing that could narrow this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Yvette Clarke, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win re-election in this Brooklyn-based district. The seat sits in territory that leans Democratic by more than twenty points, and Clarke has raised over $1 million for the campaign while benefiting from outside support on her behalf. Her Republican challenger, Joel Azumah, has no reported fundraising.

No public general-election polling or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance. Prediction markets put Clarke's chances at roughly 96%, in line with the structural advantages she holds. Barring an unforeseen development, this race is expected to remain firmly in the Democratic column.
